ai.title: Refactor agent templates to generic naming
ai.summary: Agent template identifiers in `backend/src/templates/agent-list.ts` and related files replace model-specific names (e.g., `gemini25pro_base`) with generic roles (e.g., `base`, `ask`, `thinker`). This decouples template definitions from underlying model versions, allowing easier model swaps without renaming logic. The change spans core backend files including `main-prompt.ts`, `run-agent-step.ts`, and individual agent definition files. A guard clause in `run-agent-step.ts` now throws a descriptive error if a template type is missing.

eli5.text: The system that powers AI assistants has been reorganized so that each assistant is now defined by its role (like 'ask' or 'thinker') instead of being tied to a specific AI model like 'Gemini 2.5 Pro'. This makes it easier to swap out which AI powers each assistant without needing to hunt down and change configuration references everywhere. If an assistant setup goes missing, you'll now see a clear error message explaining exactly which one is missing instead of a confusing breakdown.

ai.title: Switch eval agent to base template
ai.summary: Agent type in `run-git-evals.ts` changed from `AgentTemplateTypes.claude4_base` to `AgentTemplateTypes.base`. This internal modification affects the specific agent template used during git evaluation runs.

eli5.text: The tool that checks code changes now uses a simpler, more generic version of the assistant during its reviews, rather than a version specifically tuned for a particular model. If you were watching one of those automated code checks run, you might notice it follows a slightly different internal prompt, but the actual code review results it produces for your repositories should look the same. This change went live today for the internal evaluation runs only.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.429 release
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.429 in npm-app/release/package.json. No functional code changes, only metadata update. Scope limited to package.json.

eli5.text: Nothing changed for you right now. This release only updates the version number that tools and systems use to track the software, so they stay in sync. There are no new features or bug fixes to try out.

ai.title: Analytics init no longer throws, referral HTTP 429 to 409
ai.summary: Analytics client init and event tracking now warn and skip on missing PostHog env vars or init failure instead of throwing. Referral redemption conflict responses changed from 429 to 409. Server init continues without analytics on failure. Affects common/src/analytics.ts, web/src/app/api/referrals/helpers.ts, web/src/lib/server-init.ts.

eli5.text: When you try to redeem a referral code that has already been used, the system now correctly tells you the request conflicts with an existing referral instead of saying you're being rate limited. The analytics tracking that records events behind the scenes (like usage data) will now quietly skip recording if any required settings are missing, instead of stopping the entire application from starting up. This means the website continues to work normally even if analytics setup fails for any reason.

ai.title: Remove backend Jest config and setup
ai.summary: Deleted backend/jest.config.js and backend/jest.setup.js. Removes ts-jest preset, node test environment, and dotenv setup for backend tests. Internal cleanup of unused test infrastructure.

eli5.text: The team removed an old testing setup that was used behind the scenes to check that parts of the backend work correctly. This setup included configuration files that handled how tests run and how environment variables are loaded during development. You won't notice anything different - it doesn't affect how the app works for you. It's just internal cleanup of tools developers used during development, and since nothing depends on it anymore, it was deleted.

ai.title: Delete check-new-files-necessary integration test
ai.summary: Removed `backend/src/__tests__/check-new-files-necessary.integration.test.ts`. The 179-line suite covered `checkNewFilesNecessary` logic for file loading decisions. Deletion streamlines the repo by dropping redundant coverage for this internal helper.

eli5.text: The test file that checked whether the assistant correctly decides it needs to load new files for a request to load new files has been deleted. This was an automated check used by developers to make sure that decision logic still works as expected; for example, the test would verify the assistant says "yes I need these files" when you start a new task, and "no I don't" when you ask a follow-up question. Deleting the test file does not change how the assistant behaves for regular users - it simply removes a safety net that developers had in place to catch bugs during development. Since this test suite is now gone, developers will no longer have those specific automated checks running when they update this code. This change is already live today.

ai.title: Inject short tool and agent instructions per user step
ai.summary: getAgentPrompt now appends short tool and spawnable agent instructions to userInputPrompt. buildShortToolDescription and buildSpawnableAgentsDescription added in backend/src/tools.ts. Refactors promptType signature in backend/src/templates/strings.ts and backend/src/run-agent-step.ts.

eli5.text: Each time you ask the assistant to do something new, it now gets a brief reminder of which tools it has available right at that moment, rather than relying on a longer, general-purpose list. This makes the instructions it receives more pointed and up-to-date for the specific step you're on. You, as a reader, wouldn't see the code, but you would notice the assistant responding more consistently with the tools relevant to your current request.
